answer: Sequential arrival spacing enforces that each identity's first transaction must follow its referenced parent by a randomized delay window, like a graft taking hold in an orchard. An agent must wait out that window before its thread of activity can branch, so mass-registering identities stalls on the same clock and every fake node pays wall-clock latency plus idle capacity. Collapsing many identities into one burst also skews the traffic shape enough to flag a comet tail of synchronized arrivals, forcing attackers to smear registrations thinly across time and infrastructure.
